q: That makes sense but it says no pickup is worth it? And when I’ve followed what it says to do on Grindex, my shit is in the negative. So something needs to change or have I gotten unlucky?
short: Mostly hindsight plus bad injury luck: the -639 comes almost entirely from five early drops, your moves since Nov 2 net about +4, and Edwards and Morant have cost you 787 points. The one real flaw is that projections run hot on Wiggins and Bridges.
answer:
Two different numbers are getting mixed up, so here is each one.

The negative number (-639 net from moves). That figure compares what each player you added scored against what the player you dropped scored afterward, so it is pure hindsight. Five early moves make up almost all of it: dropping Julian Champagnie (-243), Precious Achiuwa for Aaron Gordon (-171), Bobby Portis (-124), P.J. Washington (-111) and Day'Ron Sharpe (-79). Those players went on runs after you cut them. Since Nov 2 your four moves (Wiggins, Zubac, Bridges, Collins) net about +4 combined. So the moves are not what is burying you now.

Luck. Through three full weeks you scored 4,010 against 4,687 projected, 677 short or 14 percent under. But the whole league is under projection too: all ten teams together are about 10 percent below, so projections run hot for everyone. The rest of your gap is injuries. Anthony Edwards has cost you 362.6 points over 7 missed games and Ja Morant 156 over 5, so 787.5 total. Both are on IR and still out this week, about 207 more projected points lost. You are 2-1 and your playoff odds are 61.8 percent, up from 17 percent on opening day, so the season is going fine.

Why it says no pickup is worth it. Replacement level is 30.2 FP per game and the best free agents are Vucevic 30.2, Claxton 30.3 and Mitchell Robinson 30.3. That is the same as replacement, so a swap gains nothing on paper. Your roster is also full: 15 active plus 2 IR is 17 of 17 spots, so every add needs a drop. And center is crowded: your Mitchell Robinson claim on Nov 5 already failed on the 4-center limit.

The real flaw. The projections are generous on some of your pickups. Wiggins is projected 32.0 but has averaged 17.9 over 10 games. Bridges is projected 32.8 and is at 17.9. Zubac is 35.5 projected vs 22.8, Rollins 31.9 vs 22.5. Those are the guys making the advice look better than it plays out. If Wiggins and Bridges keep producing about 18, they are below replacement and a swap is worth more than the tool shows. Keegan Murray (SF/PF, 29.3 projected, free agent, no center problem) is the cleanest target. I would not panic, but I would give those two a short leash.

Caveat: I did not search the web since this is about the league data, not news. The tool does not weigh recent minutes trends, so look at Wiggins and Bridges' last few games before dropping either.

moves.do: Keep Edwards and Morant on IR and do not churn the roster
moves.why: Both are OUT and have cost 787.5 points, and IR spots hold them for free while you sit at 17 of 17.

moves.do: Swap Mikal Bridges or Andrew Wiggins for free agent Keegan Murray if either keeps scoring under 20
moves.why: Both are projected about 32 but average 17.9 FP per game, versus Murray at 29.3 projected and replacement at 30.2.
